key_insight: LLM agents can act as reliable natural-language schedulers for home energy management, achieving near-MILP performance when connected to live tools and function-calling APIs.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical pathway to reduce the user-interface burden in HEMS by translating household preferences into actionable, cost-aware appliance schedules.
method: Built a tool-calling ReAct agent for multi-appliance scheduling
Integrated live Octopus Agile prices, weather, PV estimates, household usage data, and retrieval-augmented knowledge
Benchmarked GPT-4o-mini, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and Claude Sonnet 4.6 against MILP ground truth across conflicts and week-long deployment
evidence_signal: Across tariff-day tests, constraint conflicts, solar-aware co-optimization, and week-long deployment, native function calling yielded 100% scheduling success and 96.7-98.0% of oracle savings.
watch_item: Performance drops sharply with text-parsed action interfaces, so robust function-calling and guardrails are critical for deployment reliability.
paper_title: LLMs for Agentic Home Energy Management
